name: Pronomen
subtitle: Pronouns: mig/honom, min/mitt/mina, sin vs hans, reflexive verbs

ruleCards.title: Subject or object?
ruleCards.rule: The subject form does the action. After the verb, or after a preposition like med, till or för, use the object form.
ruleCards.watch: Mig, dig and sig are written with g but usually said “mej, dej, sej”.

fun.sv: Jag ser honom. Han ser mig. Ingen av oss säger hej.
fun.en: I see him. He sees me. Neither of us says hello.

ruleCards.title: The pronoun pairs
ruleCards.rule: Every subject pronoun has an object form. Learn them as pairs.
ruleCards.watch: De and dem both sound like “dom”, so think: does it do the action (de) or does something happen to it (dem)?

fun.sv: – Jag älskar dig, sa jag till kaffet. Det värmde mig.
fun.en: “I love you,” I said to the coffee. It warmed me.

ruleCards.title: Min, mitt, mina
ruleCards.rule: My, your (one person), our and your (plural) change like en/ett/plural, following the noun that is owned.
ruleCards.watch: The noun after a possessive has no ending: min bil, not min bilen.

fun.sv: Min soffa, mitt täcke, mina kuddar. Allt är kattens.
fun.en: My sofa, my duvet, my pillows. It all belongs to the cat.

ruleCards.title: Hans, hennes, deras
ruleCards.rule: His, her and their never change, whatever the noun is.
ruleCards.watch: Hennes is already possessive. There is no extra -s.

fun.sv: Hans bil, hennes bil, deras bil. Det är samma bil.
fun.en: His car, her car, their car. It’s the same car.

ruleCards.title: Sin, sitt, sina: “his/her/their own”
ruleCards.rule: When the owner is the third-person subject (han, hon, de, a name, man) of the same clause, use sin/sitt/sina. If it belongs to someone else, use hans/hennes/deras. Sin/sitt/sina change like en/ett/plural.
ruleCards.watch: Sin is never part of the subject: Erik och hans fru bor här (not sin fru). With jag, du, vi, ni use min, din, vår, er.

fun.sv: Katten har sin säng, sin mat och sina leksaker. Men den sover i min säng.
fun.en: The cat has its own bed, its own food and its own toys. But it sleeps in my bed.

ruleCards.title: Reflexive verbs
ruleCards.rule: Some verbs need a pronoun that points back to the subject: jag – mig, du – dig, han/hon/man – sig, vi – oss, ni – er, de – sig.
examples: De ska gifta sig i juni.
ruleCards.watch: With de, the reflexive is sig, not dem: De gifter sig.

fun.sv: Jag lägger mig klockan tio. Katten lägger sig på mig klockan fem över tio.
fun.en: I go to bed at ten. The cat lies down on me at five past ten.

ruleCards.title: Man: “one, you, people”
ruleCards.rule: Use man for general statements about people. The verb looks the same as with han or hon.
examples: You’re not allowed to smoke here.
I Finland dricker man mycket kaffe.
In Finland people drink a lot of coffee.
ruleCards.watch: Man goes with sig and sin: Man måste ta hand om sig.

fun.sv: I Finland står man två meter från varandra i busskön.
fun.en: In Finland people stand two metres apart in the bus queue.
